2519	    # -- atomic batch rotation --------------------------------------------
2520	    # A batch rotates 1-100 existing keys of one tenant as one logical
2521	    # transaction: every key lock is taken first (sorted by key_id, shared
2522	    # deadline), every new version is minted and every file lands carrying the
2523	    # SAME pending marker, and a single batch_rotate audit event (key_id null)
2524	    # is the commit point. A crash/failure before that append restores every
2525	    # file to its pre-batch bytes and deletes every minted handle. Two durable
2526	    # artifacts make recovery exact:
2527	    #   * the provision journal provisions/<event_id>.json records every
2528	    #     minted handle as it appears (shared with rotate/import/restore);
2529	    #   * the snapshot journal batch-rotations/<event_id>.json records every
2530	    #     key's pre-batch file bytes, so an uncommitted group can always be
2531	    #     restored even when this frame no longer holds them.
2532	    BATCH_ROTATED = "rotated"
2533	    BATCH_NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
2534	    _BATCH_DIR = "batch-rotations"
2535	
2536	    def _batch_snapshot_path(self, snapshot_id: str) -> str:
2537	        return os.path.join(
2538	            self.data_dir, self._BATCH_DIR, snapshot_id + ".json"
2539	        )

2541	    def _write_batch_snapshot(
2542	        self, snapshot_id: str, tenant_id: str, key_ids: List[str],
2543	        previous_bytes: dict,
2544	    ) -> None:
2545	        """Durably record the pre-batch whole-file bytes of every group key.
2546	
2547	        ``previous_bytes`` maps key_id to the key file's literal bytes read
2548	        before the batch. They are stored base64-encoded, so crash recovery
2549	        of an uncommitted group restores each file byte-for-byte rather than
2550	        re-serializing a parsed object. Written before any provider call; a
2551	        group whose snapshot is gone is left untouched rather than guessed at.
2552	        """
2553	        directory = os.path.join(self.data_dir, self._BATCH_DIR)
2554	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
2555	        path = self._batch_snapshot_path(snapshot_id)
2556	        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
2557	        payload = {
2558	            "event_id": snapshot_id,
2559	            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
2560	            "keys": [
2561	                {
2562	                    "key_id": key_id,
2563	                    "previous_b64": base64.b64encode(
2564	                        previous_bytes[key_id]
2565	                    ).decode("ascii"),
2566	                }
2567	                for key_id in key_ids
2568	            ],
2569	        }
2570	        try:
2571	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
2572	                json.dump(payload, fh)
2573	                fh.flush()
2574	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
2575	        except BaseException:
2576	            # The durable snapshot never landed and no key file references
2577	            # it yet (it is written before any provider call); remove the
2578	            # partial file so a corrupt snapshot cannot outlive the attempt.
2579	            # A failed unlink simply leaves it for the next open, whose
2580	            # corrupt-snapshot rule preserves the scene rather than guessing.
2581	            try:
2582	                os.unlink(path)
2583	            except OSError:
2584	                pass
2585	            raise

2587	    def _read_batch_snapshot(self, snapshot_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
2588	        try:
2589	            with open(
2590	                self._batch_snapshot_path(snapshot_id), "r", encoding="utf-8"
2591	            ) as fh:
2592	                data = json.load(fh)
2593	        except (OSError, ValueError):
2594	            return None
2595	        if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(
2596	            data.get("keys"), list
2597	        ):
2598	            return None
2599	        return data
